e.etymology: From the biblical Plain of Sharon, the fertile coastal plain of Israel, praised in the Song of Solomon's rose of Sharon. It became an English given name in the 20th century.
namesakes: Sharon Stone (actress in Basic Instinct)
Sharon Osbourne (TV personality and music manager)
Sharon Tate (actress murdered by the Manson family)

assoc.t: rose of Sharon, a biblical phrase and flowering shrub

e.meaning: of Mars, the Roman god of war
e.etymology: The French and Catalan form of Mark, from the Roman first name Marcus, probably derived from Mars, the god of war.
namesakes: Marc Anthony (salsa and pop singer)
Marc Jacobs (fashion designer)
Marc Chagall (painter)

assoc.t: Marc Jacobs, fashion and handbag label

e.etymology: From Reginaldus, a Latin form of the Germanic name behind Reynold and Ronald: ragin (counsel) plus wald (rule). The spelling was shaped by Latin regina, queen.
namesakes: Reggie Jackson (Hall of Fame slugger, born Reginald)
Elton John (born Reginald Dwight)
Reginald VelJohnson (Carl Winslow on Family Matters)

e.etymology: The Spanish feminine of Juan (John), from Latin Johanna and Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. It matches English Jane, Joan and Joanna.
namesakes: Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz (17th-century Mexican poet and nun)
e.note: Sounds like the end of marijuana, which invites jokes in English.

e.etymology: A spelling of Jaylynn, a modern American coinage that joins Jay or Jae to the -lynn ending.
The Spanish form of Jesse, from Hebrew Yishai, the father of King David in the Bible. The Hebrew name is often explained as gift.
From Hebrew tzvi, gazelle, an animal the Bible uses as an image of beauty and swiftness. It is traditionally paired with the Yiddish name Hirsch, deer.
e.note: The opening tsv sound is hard for most English speakers to say.

e.etymology: From Old English Raedwulf and Old Norse Rathulfr, counsel plus wolf, reinforced by the Norman form Radulf. The older English pronunciation, still heard in Britain, is Rafe.
namesakes: Ralph Lauren (fashion designer)
Ralph Waldo Emerson (essayist and poet)
Ralph Macchio (star of The Karate Kid)

assoc.t: Wreck-It Ralph, Disney's video game bad guy
to ralph: slang for vomiting
Ralph Lauren, fashion house behind Polo
Ralphs, Southern California supermarket chain

e.note: Ralph is American slang for vomiting.

e.etymology: From Turkish aydin, bright or enlightened, a name since at least the 13th century. In the US it is also used as a spelling of Aiden, an unrelated Irish name.
A K spelling of Cross, the English word and the surname for someone who lived near a stone cross, used as a given name with Christian overtones.

assoc.t: Kris Kross, 1990s rap duo behind Jump

e.etymology: The usual European form of the biblical Dinah, from a Hebrew root meaning to judge. In Italian it is also a short form of names ending in -dina, such as Claudina.
namesakes: Dinah (daughter of Jacob and Leah in Genesis)

e.etymology: From the linden or lime tree, and from surnames in English, Dutch, German and Swedish built on the same word. Lyndon is the related English surname.

assoc.t: linden, a shade tree with fragrant flowers

e.etymology: From Greek Ariadne, explained by ancient scholars as Cretan ari (very) plus adnos (holy). In myth she gave Theseus the thread that led him out of the Minotaur's Labyrinth.
namesakes: Ariadne (Cretan princess who helped Theseus escape the Labyrinth)
Ariadne (the dream architect played by Elliot Page in Inception)

e.etymology: From Arabic diya, light or radiance, a traditional male name across the Muslim world. In the US it is given mostly to girls, alongside Mia, Gia and Tia.

assoc.t: Zia sun symbol on the New Mexico state flag
Italian word for aunt

e.etymology: The English tree name, from Old English mapul, used as a surname and in recent years as a girls' name alongside Hazel, Willow and Juniper.

assoc.t: maple tree, maple syrup and Canada's maple leaf

e.etymology: From Sanskrit jaya, victory, a common Indian boys' name also written Jay. In the US it is used as well as a spelling of the English nickname Jay.
The Italian and Spanish form of Seraphina, from the seraphim, the highest order of angels, whose Hebrew name means burning ones. Saint Serafina (Fina) of San Gimignano bore it in the 13th century.
namesakes: Serafina Pekkala (witch queen in Philip Pullman's His Dark Materials)

e.etymology: The Spanish name of Greece, from Latin Graecia, used as a girls' name in Mexico and other Spanish-speaking countries.

assoc.t: Spanish name for the country Greece

e.note: English speakers often read it as GREE-shuh; in Spanish it is GREH-see-ah.

e.etymology: From the English seaside city, a clipping of Brighthelmstone, Old English for the farm of a man named Beorhthelm. Many hear it simply as bright town.

assoc.t: seaside resort city on England's south coast
Brighton, maker of handbags and silver jewelry
Brighton ski resort in Utah

e.etymology: A form of Irish Cillian, probably from cill, church, with a diminutive ending. The single-l spelling is standard in Germany, where the Irish missionary Saint Kilian is patron of Wurzburg.

assoc.t: Kilian Paris, luxury perfume house

e.etymology: Two sources: the byname of the 13th-century Persian poet Jalal al-Din Rumi, meaning from Rum (Anatolia), and a Japanese girls' name whose meaning depends on the characters, often including beauty.
namesakes: Rumi (13th-century Persian Sufi poet)
Rumi Carter (daughter of Beyonce and Jay-Z)

assoc.t: Rumi, 13th-century Persian Sufi poet
Rumi, lead singer of Huntr/x in KPop Demon Hunters

e.etymology: From the surname, in most cases a form of baron, the Anglo-Norman title of nobility. As an Irish surname it comes from O Bearain, from a word for spear.
namesakes: Barron Trump (youngest son of Donald Trump)
Barron Hilton (hotel magnate)

assoc.t: Barron Trump, son of President Donald Trump
Barron's, financial weekly

e.note: Closely tied to Barron Trump since 2016. It also sounds the same as the word barren.

e.etymology: A respelling of Nevaeh, which is heaven written backward and took off after the singer Sonny Sandoval of P.O.D. gave it to his daughter in 2000.
e.note: This spelling reverses to haeven, not heaven; Nevaeh is the form that works.

e.etymology: A modern American name that sits between Armani, the Italian fashion surname, and Harmony.
From Russian Sonya, the pet form of Sofiya (Sophia), from Greek sophia, wisdom. Russian novels brought it into English and the Romance languages.
namesakes: Sonia Sotomayor (US Supreme Court justice)
Sonia Gandhi (Indian political leader)

e.etymology: A pet form of Cassandra, the Trojan prophetess of Greek myth, and of Cassidy, an Irish surname. It has been given as a name in its own right since the 19th century.
namesakes: Cassie Ventura (R&B singer of Me & U, known as Cassie)
Cassie Howard (Sydney Sweeney's character in Euphoria)

assoc.t: R&B singer Cassie (Cassie Ventura)

e.etymology: A spelling of Leilani, from Hawaiian lei (a garland of flowers, and by extension a beloved child) plus lani (sky, heaven, royal).
A spelling of Ayla, which has two sources: Turkish ayla, the halo around the moon, and Hebrew Elah, an oak or terebinth tree. Jean Auel's heroine in The Clan of the Cave Bear spread it in English.
As a Hebrew name, a form of Aryeh, lion. As a Dutch name, a short form of Adriaan (Adrian). For American girls it also works as a short form of Ariana or Ariel.
namesakes: Arie Luyendyk Jr. (race car driver and star of The Bachelor)
India.Arie (Grammy-winning soul singer)

e.etymology: A form of Denzil, a Cornish surname from the manor of Denzell in Cornwall; the meaning of the place name is unclear. Its American use follows the actor Denzel Washington.
namesakes: Denzel Washington (Oscar-winning actor)
Denzel Curry (rapper)

assoc.t: actor Denzel Washington

e.etymology: A spelling of Evelyn, also read as Eva plus Lyn. Evelyn began as an English surname from the Norman girls' name Aveline.
In Greek, a short form of Aristides or Aristotelis, both built on aristos, best, and the modern Greek form of Ares, the god of war. In the US it is also given to girls.
